What part of the world are you in? I'm interested to know how landscapers are doing out here in California as far as turf reduction, artificial turfs, and native landscapes due to the drought and all. If anyone could shed some light.
I'm down in the deep south. Mississippi. We are having a serious heat wave. Actual high today, 98F with a heat index of 110F.

I am a So Cal landscaper.

I wont touch artificial turf. I don't like it so I wont do it.

I have been actively lobbying a few of my customers to remove turf and have had a few jobs. Most people seem to be content with some dead spots this year however.

My basic go to plan for removing turf is to replace it with pathway and planters on low pressure drip. I don't really try to push native plants, I have found that lavenders and sages are really nice and preform as well as any native plants. Ceanothus is an exception, I just love that stuff on slopes and as a ground cover. For best results plant in fall and set up overhead irrigation. Water one day a week max... nothing in summer (plant is dormant). If the homeowner is willing to keep and eye on it no irrigation is needed.

I was doing some work on golf courses in the area (also SoCal) and while the company was a landscaping company the name of the game at every course seems to be water reduction and turf elimination. This leads me to believe there must be some sort of wave going through on the residential level as well. I only wish I had the knowledge and experience to feel confident enough to start a business, I'd be all over that. Am I mistaken? It's summertime and time to get outside and have fun! What do you guys do to stay in shape and have fun at the same time?
Hey Voaters! What do you guys do to stay in shape and have fun?
I love to bike everywhere. Save tons of money on gas (even when it's this cheap), and spend time outside and get a workout anytime you leave the house.

I love swimming. Im not in shape at all, im currently trying to lose weight, but swimming is fun and easy exercise. Since your already by the beach just drag a few friends along and barbecue as-well.

Also walking alone is incredibly liberating, especially in a forest or similar. I try to do it every other day, it really helps my depression and alleviates sleeping issues.

Swimming is my favorite! My mom owns a house with a big lake right by it so I go and visit every weekend and go swimming with her.

I also agree that walking helps a lot! I struggle with depression and bipolar and when I get too wound up I just go from a walk around town to let my mind wander and de-stress

I go to the gym. It's fun for me as I'm super competitive, have some friends that also lift and it happens to get sunlight most afternoons thanks to its very large windows, great in summer! I also like to take my bike out on a new adventure if it's sunny. I basically throw up Google maps, look for a park I haven't been to, get directions and head off. Normally I get lost and end up going somewhere else but it's always good fun and I get to see something new. What do you do?

I've actually been considering getting a gym membership for this exact reason. Right now I just walk around town and go swimming at a lake on weekends but I'm really trying to get more active. It's fun lounging around sometimes, but definitely not all the time.

Sword fighting. I got into longsword fencing via Historical European Martial Arts (HEMA). It is a full contact sport based on 14-18th century fighting manuals. It can definitely be a workout plus you get to learn how to really handle a sword.

This is a look at what it basically is. I have not started competing yet, but I participate in informal fights with friends.

I like rock climbing but since I'm new to it, it's more like wall climbing with a harness and hard plastic rocks.

I like to go geocaching. It keep me busy and is a great excuse to get outside. Plus, there's treasure at the end!
I've heard of this but have never really tried it. Is there really stuff hidden everywhere for me to find?!

Yes, everywhere (depending on location)! Check out /v/geocaching and geocaching.com, I bet there is one in your neighborhood. They can range in size from a tiny one where you only write your name, to a huge one with logs of treasures. Good luck, and don't forget your pen!

I like to exercise while I game so I can marathon without having spent all day sitting on my ass. Cooking a stack of rocks in minecraft...time for squats. Queuing for an online match...I let me pick up my weights in the meantime. Also like to walk since my town is safe enough for me to walk alone and when I get the chance I go to romp in lava fields.

I do Krav Maga - Israeli defense force fighting style. It's really intense and I always end up bruised up but it's so fun. I'm a petite female, so it gives me a sense of power that I know I could beat up the average person, whatever their size. My favorite is when we have knife fights.

I'm lucky enough to have a few pretty good hiking spots near where I live. some of them are good for quick 1-2 hour hikes and others I can wander in from sunup to sundown (or until my water runs out), the manzanita trees in one of the hiking trails are peeling right now (don't know enough about how the trees work to know what it's called or why) and that shit is beautiful, looks like the trees are fire frozen in time.

Best part about hiking in getting to the top of somewhere and enjoying the view. It's probably a skewed perspective but the views look more awesome because I sweated my balls off working to earn them, and if I was given the opportunity to be driven to the tops I'd say no, nothing beats being at the very end of your endurance and cresting a slope to see a vista with absolutely no sign of human interference laid out for your enjoyment. Sipping water and smoking while you rest up, looking at trees and rocks and rivers, feeling your energy slowly returning like the place itself is recharging you so that you can hike another ten miles back to your car free from the stink of humanity, and knowing that you can do it again some other time. Wouldn't trade it for the world.
